newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sells 90 bln bolivars of TEM bills.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sells 90 bln bolivars of TEM bills.

text.p: Venezuela's Central Bank said it sold 60 billion bolivars of 173-day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills at a price of 100.58 pct.
The 173-day bills carried a 30.66 percent coupon.

The bank also sold 15 billion bolivars of 262-day notes with a 31.79 percent coupon at a price of 98.92 percent, and 15 billion bolivars of 351-day notes with a 32.99 percent coupon at an average price of 98.19 percent.

According to a preliminary calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula, the yield on the notes fell to 29.27 percent for the 173-day TEMs, to 33.64 percent for the 262-day notes, and to 35.50 percent for the 351-day TEMs.
Yields for benchmark six-month TEMs sold at last week's auction were 30.75 percent, while yields on one-year paper stood at 37.79 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
